title: A private network with controlled egress
summary: 40 high schools in Jalisco publish grades on a portal. The state Education Ministry requires that neither the servers nor the database can be reached from the internet.

requirements.1: {{s1}} lets the private servers download patches from the internet, but nobody outside can open a connection to them.
requirements.2: All outbound web traffic goes through {{s2}}, an intermediary that only lets it reach the domains of the SAT, the bank and the patch repository.
requirements.3: {{s3}} is associated with the database subnet and its rules only let the app servers in on port 3306; the reply comes back on its own, with no extra rule.
requirements.4: {{s4}} gives administrators a terminal on servers with no public IP, without opening port 22 to the internet, and keeps a record of every session.
requirements.5: {{s5}} takes the PDF report cards from the servers to object storage without going out to the internet or through slot 1.
requirements.6: {{s6}} keeps the source, destination and port of the servers' network traffic to investigate a scan.
requirements.7: The grades database listens on port 3306 and lives in a private subnet, with no public IP.

s1.explanation: Azure NAT Gateway gives private VMs outbound internet access and does not allow unsolicited inbound connections: only packets that answer an outbound connection get through.
s1.hint_cue: nobody outside can open a connection to them

s2.explanation: Azure Firewall is a stateful firewall with central rules that can limit outbound HTTP/S traffic to a list of FQDNs, such as the SAT, bank and patch domains.
s2.hint_cue: only lets it reach the domains

s3.explanation: An NSG is associated with the subnet and its rules allow or deny traffic; with the servers' application security group as the source, only they get in on 3306. It keeps the state of each flow, so the reply passes with no extra rule.
s3.hint_cue: is associated with the database subnet

s4.explanation: Azure Bastion gives RDP and SSH over TLS from the portal to VMs with no public IP, protects them from port scanning and, with the Premium SKU, records the sessions.
s4.hint_cue: without opening port 22 to the internet

s5.explanation: The private endpoint gives the storage account a private IP from the VNet; traffic goes over Private Link on the Microsoft backbone, with no exposure to the public internet.
s5.hint_cue: without going out to the internet or through slot 1

s6.explanation: Virtual network flow logs record the IP traffic in the VNet: source and destination IP and port, protocol, and whether the flow was allowed or denied.

azure-nsg.s2: NSG rules use IP addresses, CIDR ranges, service tags or application security groups; they cannot limit egress to domain names.

azure-public-ip.s1: A public IP on the VM is another way out, but it gives the VM an address on the internet. Also, NAT Gateway takes precedence over instance-level public IPs.

azure-asg.s3: An application security group only groups the VMs' network interfaces; the rules that allow or deny traffic live in the NSG associated with the subnet, which uses the group as source or destination.

azure-vpn-gateway.s4: A point-to-site VPN creates a secure connection from one computer to the virtual network; it is not the RDP or SSH connection over TLS to each VM that Bastion provides, which records every session with the Premium SKU.

azure-vnet-peering.s5: Peering connects two or more virtual networks so their resources can communicate; the private VNet IP for the storage account comes from the private endpoint.

azure-activity-log.s6: The activity log keeps management operations on resources, such as creating a VM or changing an access policy; the source, destination and port of each flow are recorded by virtual network flow logs.
